working_title: How a Baker's Oven Toasting London in 1666 Changed Everything
hook: Imagine your entire city catching fire because a baker forgot to turn off the oven.
structure: Countdown of the key moments that led to the outcome, building tension toward the final one.

cast.look: A tired 17th-century English baker in his 40s, round face, flour-dusted apron over a brown woolen tunic, messy dark hair.

poses.panicked: staring wide-eyed at glowing embers, hands thrown up in alarm
poses.running: bolting through an open door, holding a loaf of bread, terrified expression

cast.look: An overweight, wealthy 17th-century city official in a heavy red velvet mayoral robe and white lace collar, pompous expression.

poses.dismissive: yawning, waving hand dismissively, eyes closed
poses.shocked: jaw dropped open, pointing frantically at a towering wall of fire

places.look: A cramped, dark 17th-century wooden bakery interior at midnight, glowing brick oven, sacks of flour, flickering candlelight, hand-painted gouache style in ochre and deep brick red.
Narrow, winding medieval cobbled alleyways framed by overhanging timber-framed houses nearly touching at the top, thick grey smoke billowing, warm muted palette.

scenes.narration: Imagine your entire city catching fire because a baker forgot to turn off his oven in the dead of night.

shots.fact: The Great Fire started in a bakery in Pudding Lane shortly after midnight on Sunday 2

scenes.narration: In 1666, London was a crowded maze of wooden homes with overhanging upper storeys nearly touching across narrow, winding alleys.

shots.fact: Typical multi-storey timbered London tenement houses had jetties, or projecting upper floors.

scenes.narration: The Lord Mayor hesitated in giving orders for firebreaks, letting a tiny spark become an unstoppable, roaring firestorm.

shots.fact: Lord Mayor Sir Thomas Bloodworth hesitated to order the demolition of burning buildings.
shots.bubble: A woman might piss it out!

scenes.narration: As flames devoured medieval churches and historic markets, terrified residents fled through the narrow gates of the old Roman wall.

shots.fact: The high Roman wall enclosing the city impeded escape from the inferno.

scenes.narration: Finally, the Tower of London garrison used gunpowder to blow up houses and halt the relentless spread of the flames.

shots.fact: The Tower of London garrison used gunpowder to create effective firebreaks.
